> “He who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him, and rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom’s voice” (John 7:29).

## CHAPTER XV

### From the books of the pagans

Are these things enough for you, O Jews? Are so many witnesses and testimonies from your Law and from your own people enough for you? Or will you still dare, with shameless intent [Note: [Col. 1125] The manuscripts read, “excessive shamelessness.”], to say that people of another race or nation ought to bear witness to Christ?

But if you say this, he himself indeed answers you: “I was not sent except to the sheep that had perished from the house of Israel” (Matt. 15:24). Yet just as Paul rebukes you in the Acts of the Apostles—“It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you rejected it and judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold,” he says, “we turn to the Gentiles” (Acts 13:46)—let us also demonstrate that testimony to Christ was brought forth from the Gentiles.

For truth did not remain silent, but cried out even through the tongues of its enemies. When that most eloquent poet, in the midst of his verses,

> “Now a new generation is sent down from high heaven”  
> (Virgil, *Eclogue* 4, line 7),

was he not bearing witness to Christ? Let this be called into doubt only if I bring forward other reliable witnesses from the Gentiles, saying more.

I shall not omit that king who subdued your pride by taking you captive—Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. Tell us, Nebuchadnezzar, what you saw in the furnace into which you had unjustly thrown three righteous men. Tell us, tell us what was revealed to you.

“Did we not,” he says, “throw three bound men into the furnace?” And they answer him, “Certainly, O king.” “Behold,” he says, “I see four men walking about unbound in the midst of the fire, and there is no corruption in them, and the appearance of the fourth is like the Son of God” (Dan. 3:91).

O foreigner, where did you get this? Who announced the Son of God to you? What law, what prophet? He has not yet been born into the world, yet you recognize the likeness of the one who is to be born. Where did you get this? Who announced it to you, unless divine fire so illumined you inwardly that, while the Jews—your enemies—were held captive there in your presence, you could bear witness in this way to the Son of God?

## CHAPTER XVI

### From the Sibylline prophecies

### The prophecy of the Sibyl

But because “every word stands on the testimony of two or three witnesses,” as the Lord himself says in refutation of your obstinacy, “it is written in your Law that the testimony of two men is true” (Deut. 17:6; John 8:17), let a third witness also be introduced from the Gentiles, so that the testimony of the truth may be strengthened in every respect.

Let us bring forward what the Sibyl proclaimed in prophecy even concerning Christ, so that, with one stone, the foreheads of both—Jews and pagans—may be struck, and all the enemies of Christ may be struck down by their own sword, like Goliath (1 Sam. 17:50). Hear what she said [Note: [Col. 1126] See *The City of God*, book 18, chapter 23.]:

> **Ι** The sign of judgment: the earth shall be drenched with sweat.  
> **Η** From heaven the King shall come, destined to be for all ages.  
> **Σ** Certainly present in the flesh, to judge the world.  
> **Ο** From there the unbelieving and the faithful shall see God,  
> **Υ** The Most High with the saints, at the very end of the age.  
> **Σ** Thus souls shall be present with the flesh, whom he himself judges.  
> **Χ** When the world lies uncultivated amid dense thorn bushes.  
> **Ρ** They shall cast away the images of men, and all wealth as well.  
> **Ε** Fire shall burn the lands, the sea, and the heavens,  
> **Ι** Seeking out, it shall break open the gates of gloomy Tartarus.  
> **Σ** For the free light of the saints shall then be given to all flesh,  
> **Τ** But the guilty and the eternal flame shall consume.  
> **Ο** Revealing hidden deeds, then each person shall speak  
> **Σ** Of secrets, and God shall disclose hearts to the light.  
> **Θ** Then there shall also be mourning, and all shall gnash their teeth.  
> **Ε** The sun’s radiance shall be removed, and the chorus of stars shall perish.  
> **Ο** The heavens shall be rolled up, and the moon’s splendor shall vanish.  
> **Υ** He shall cast down the hills and raise the valleys from below.  
> **Υ** Nothing among human things shall remain lofty or high.  
> **Ι** Now the mountains and the blue depths of the sea are made equal with the plains.  
> **Ο** All things shall cease; the shattered earth shall perish.  
> **Σ** Likewise the springs shall burn, and the rivers with fire.  
> **Σ** But then the trumpet shall send down a mournful sound from above,  
> **Ω** Groaning over the world’s wretched crime and its varied labors,  
> **Τ** And the earth, splitting open, shall display Tartarean chaos.  
> **Η** And here, before the Lord, the kings shall be made to stand, every one of them.  
> **Ρ** A stream of fire and sulfur shall fall from heaven.

These words concerning Christ’s birth, passion, resurrection, and second coming were composed in such a way that, if someone wishes to distinguish the initial letters of these verses in Greek, he will find:

> **Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς Θεοῦ Υἱὸς Σωτήρ**

that is, “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.” The same appears when the verses are translated into Latin, except that the distinctive character of the Greek letters could not be preserved quite so precisely.

Listen with the utmost attention to other Sibylline verses that demonstrate Christ’s passion more openly [Note: [Col. 1127] As in the preceding verses, here too we follow the ancient manuscripts, from which the printed editions differed greatly.]:

> Later he shall come into the hands of wicked unbelievers.  
> They shall strike God with unclean hands.  
> And with polluted mouths they shall spit poisonous spittle.  
> But he shall simply give his holy back to the blows.  
> Receiving blows to the face, he shall remain silent, lest anyone recognize  
> That he is the Word, or from where he came, so that he may speak to the dead.  
> And he shall be crowned with a crown of thorns.  
> As food they gave him gall, and as drink vinegar.  
> They shall display this table of inhospitality.  
> For you, foolish one, did not understand your God,  
> Who was playing with the minds of mortals [Note: [Col. 1127] The manuscripts read, “senses.”], but with thorns  
> You crowned him, and mixed the bitter gall.  
> The veil of the temple shall indeed be torn, and in the middle of the day  
> There shall be an exceedingly dark night for three hours.  
> And he shall die by death; and after receiving sleep for three days,  
> Then, returning from the dead [Note: [Col. 1127] The manuscripts read, “from the underworld.”], he shall come back to the light.  
> Recalled, he shall show the first beginning of the resurrection [Note: [Col. 1127] The manuscripts read, “when the beginning of the resurrection has been revealed, the first one recalled.”].

## CHAPTER XVII

### Testimonies from heaven, the sea, the earth, and the underworld

I believe now, O Jewish enemies, that you have been so overwhelmed and refuted by so many witnesses that you ought to seek nothing further. Yet with excessive folly, or rather madness, you yourselves knew everything that had been said and written about Christ, and nevertheless said shamelessly to the very Truth, “You bear witness about yourself; your testimony is not true” (John 8:13).

Nevertheless, so that the truth of the divine majesty may shine forth, let all creation proclaim that it has borne witness to its Creator, above the illustrious voices of so many witnesses.

Did not heaven bear witness when, in the new generation of a human being, it displayed the newly appeared star to the nations, like a tongue and finger, in the way it could, demonstrating that God had been born as man?

Did not the sea bear witness when, in a certain sense forgetting its own nature, its liquid substance assumed solidity and carried the footprints of its Lord, so that what was said might be fulfilled: “Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters” (Ps. 76:20)?

That element, wishing to show how great the difference is between creature and Creator, would have swallowed Peter in its shifting waves as he sought to walk upon it in service of Christ, unless the Lord of all things had stretched out his hand to Peter as he sank (Matt. 14:31).

Did not the earth bear witness when, sprinkled with his saliva, it was used to anoint the eyes of a man born blind and restore sight to one who could not see (John 9:7) [Note: [Col. 1127] Some manuscripts read, “displayed.”]? The Maker repaired from the earth’s clay what was lacking in the workmanship—the whole human being—that he had first formed from the earth (Gen. 2:8).

Did not the underworld bear witness to Christ when, having lost its rightful claim, it preserved intact for four days Lazarus, whom it had received to be dissolved, so that it might return him unharmed when it heard the voice of its Lord commanding (John 11:43)?

And in Christ’s very passion, shall I not summon public light itself as a witness, in a certain sense, against your shamelessness and savage madness? As you supposed, only a man, Christ, was being killed by you. Yet even if he had been merely that, you ought to have spared him, so as to keep your hands free from the blood of an innocent man.

What blindness was poured into your hearts, that even the darkness of the sun at midday did not terrify you, with the light cut off amid its bright rays? Night was hidden in the day [Note: [Col. 1127] The manuscripts read, “Night answered the day.”]; indeed, night seized the day, and nature did not preserve the course of its order. The heavens were darkened, the earth mourned, the veil of the temple was torn, the rocks were split, the underworld was opened (Matt. 27:45, 51–52); almost the whole creation trembled at Christ’s death.

Yet even amid such great things the eyes of your hearts were not opened. O Jews, the demons who possessed your hearts said, “We know who you are. Why have you come before the time to destroy us?” (Mark 1:24). And you said, “You bear witness about yourself; your testimony is not true” (John 8:13)!

## CHAPTER XVIII

### From the events

But, without understanding your own actions, you acted in support of our cause. In the end, your wickedness served our salvation. He who had come to die for us was not frightened as a man by the mad cries of those shouting, “Crucify him, crucify him” (Luke 23:21), because as God he had foreseen them beforehand.

How you labored to corrupt the disciple Judas with money (Matt. 26:15), and to purchase Christ—from an evil seller, as evil buyers—so that he might not be possessed, conducting a wicked market in your own soul when you paid the price of our salvation!

How you labored to crush the judge who was washing his hands of your crime, by means of accusations and by invoking Caesar’s name, so that he might fulfill what you wanted done (ibid. 27:24)!

How you labored so that Christ might be killed and the robber released (ibid., 20–26)! How you labored so that Christ might suffer insults, be crowned with thorns (Mark 15:17), be hung upon the wood, and be pierced with a spear (John 19:34)! How you shouted, how you sweated, how you labored!

But all this labor of yours is our fruit. In the end, Christ is killed by you and rises for us; he is hung by you on the wood, held upon the cross, fastened with nails, and found by our leaders, his disciples, among them, with the doors shut (ibid. 20:19).

By bribing the soldiers, you wished to suppress Christ’s resurrection (Matt. 28:12–13), and behold, his resurrection is now celebrated throughout the whole world, while you have completely lost what you gave. You could not accomplish what you wanted. Hear now what you do not wish to hear:

> Rising from the dead on the third day, he was taken up into heaven and sits at the right hand of the Father (Mark 16:19; Luke 24:51).

He scattered you throughout all the lands so that everywhere you might carry the prophecies concerning his birth, passion, resurrection, and ascension—whatever had been foretold—and might minister the lamp of the Law to the nations, like wooden lampstands devoid of understanding.

Understand that this happened so that the nations, when all these events were preached, might not say that they had been fabricated by us. The prophet David also declares that this very dispersion of yours had been foretold:

> “Do not kill them, lest they at some time forget your Law; but scatter them by your power” (Ps. 58:12).

This dispersion of yours therefore bears witness to Christ, to whom you said, “You bear witness about yourself; your testimony is not true” (John 8:13). Thus, from the testimony of you, his enemies, other enemies may be confounded—those who say that Christ performed all the miracles he performed by magical arts.

They also insist that the fact that a dead man is worshiped must be attributed to magical power. Bring forth the prophetic books, O Jews, enemies of Christ, so that by them other pagan enemies may also be convicted. Long before he was born, he sent the prophets ahead of him, and they foretold everything we have discussed above.

Now judge, you who think rightly: if he used magical arts to cause himself to be worshiped even after death, was he a magician before he was born [Note: [Col. 1128] So the manuscripts read, in accordance with Augustine, *On the Harmony of the Evangelists*, book 1, chapter 11. The printed editions read, “he had sent magicians before he was born.”]?

Be confounded and corrected, you who think, believe, or say such things about Christ. And be confounded also, you Jews, who, holding the lamp of the Law in your hands, provide light to others while taking no care to look into it yourselves. You too await the coming of the one who is to come.

And he will come—but he will not come as you wish. The exalted one who was killed by you, though guilty of no crime, will come. God will come openly, and you will see him judging—the one whom you despised while he performed miracles. What will your conscience be like then, when he will show you no further patience, because he finds you dead in soul—the one who is to come to judge the living and the dead?

## CHAPTER XIX
## Against the Arians

We believe in the Holy Spirit, whom we believe to be God, equal to the Father and the Son, abiding in the Father and the Son, inseparable from the Father [Col. 1129] and the Son, reigning with the Father and the Son. The Trinity is one, and the Holy Spirit is the third person in the unity, who works all things in all.

The Arians also blaspheme him, wishing him to be inferior to the Father and the Son. Nor does that evangelical warning restrain their error, when it says: “If anyone speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but if anyone speaks a word against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this age or in the age to come” (Matt. 12:32).

What is this, Arius? Do you perceive how far your monstrousness has advanced? You speak a word against the Son of Man, because you assert that the Son of God is inferior according to his divinity. You speak a word against the Holy Spirit, making him, within that very indivisible unity, inferior even to the Son. By speaking such a word about the Word, such a word about the Holy Spirit, your sins are not forgiven either in this age or in the age to come—and you, by rebaptizing, promise to forgive the sins of others?

We acknowledge that the gift of the Holy Spirit is the remission of all sins, with the Truth itself supporting us; after his resurrection he said to his disciples: “Receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven” (John 20:23).

But you, by sacrilegious audacity, although Christ through the gift of the Holy Spirit in Baptism has already completely remitted in those baptized both original and personal sins, breathe Christ out upon the baptized and reject the Holy Spirit. You strive not to wash the reborn, but to defile them; not to liberate them, but to bind them; not to give them life, but to put them to death.

Nor is it surprising that you build these ruins day after day, since you refused to have Christ, the unbroken rock, as your foundation. Truth separates her children from your error, cherishing them so as to nourish them—not as you, by flattering them, deceive them in order to destroy them.

## CHAPTER XX

### The Resurrection

Beloved, know that within the Catholic Church alone there is true faith, genuine peace, and perpetual salvation. For it is not confined to a corner, but is wholly present everywhere. If anyone departs from it and gives himself over to the error of heretics, he will be judged like a runaway slave, not like an adopted son; he will rise not to eternal life, but rather to condemnation.

For resurrection is promised both to the good and to the wicked: “We shall all rise,” says the Apostle, “but we shall not all be changed” (1 Cor. 15:51). And what benefit is it, my brothers, to rise and not be changed? For whoever has not been changed in that life is found to have been condemned by the just Judge. But the condemned person does not attain eternal life, since he was unwilling [Note: [Col. 1129] The Ambrosian and Erasmian editions and certain manuscripts: “was not able.”] to receive the palm of victory over the hostile devil.

For what benefit is it if the devil does not hold someone in those bonds through the worship of idols, yet possesses him after he has been caught and held fast in the birdlime of heretics? Whoever wishes to reach eternal life must keep vigilant and steadfast against all the devil’s snares. For that life will not be found to be as this life is.

## CHAPTER XXI

### The Difference between Temporal and Eternal Life

Your Charity ought to know how great the difference is between this life and that one. Here there is falsehood; there, truth. Here, disturbance; there, faithful possession. Here, the worst bitterness; there, everlasting sweetness. Here, dangerous exaltation; there, secure rejoicing. Here, one fears that someone who was a friend may suddenly become an enemy; there, a friend always remains a friend, because no enemy is admitted there. Here, whatever is good is feared lest it perish; there, whatever you have received will be preserved by him who makes it possible both for you not to pass away and for what you have received not to be lost. Here, death; there, life. Here, mourning; there, joy. Here, all the things God created; there, God himself in place of all things and in all things—and whatever things may rightly be said, if indeed any words can suffice.

For the human tongue is not sufficient to praise what mortal understanding cannot comprehend. We shall come there, my brothers; and there we shall see what the eye has not seen here, there we shall hear what the ear has not heard here, there we shall understand what the human heart has not been able to comprehend here (1 Cor. 2:9), seeing and enjoying, we shall rejoice with indescribable joy (1 Pet. 1:8).

And what joy there will be where there is no fear! What joy there will be when you see yourself a companion of the angels, a participant in the kingdom of heaven, reigning with the King, possessing everything by desiring nothing, rich without greed, administering without money, judging without a successor, reigning without fear of barbarians, living without death in eternal life!

## CHAPTER XXII

### The Way to the Homeland

But in order that we may come to these things, let us not abandon the safest way that leads there. What is this way? Christ in his entirety, both head and body. As head, the equal Son, abiding in the One who remains; as body, inferior, swiftly traversing this way like a giant (Ps. 18:6). The head and the body: Christ and the Church.

Let us not separate ourselves from him by believing something else about him, as the heretics do; nor from her by deviating through our wicked conduct. She is the true mother, the devout and chaste mother, adorned inwardly with the dignity of her husband, not outwardly and shamefully colored by deceptive falsehood.

Let no foreign name, fabricated against this mother, lead you astray; let no alien appearance of the Church deceive you. She is not the bride of Christ who does not acknowledge her husband. She is disgraceful who strives by her words to tarnish the appearance of so great a husband; she falsely assumes the name of the Church.

I see you indeed, O deceitful cave [Note: [Col. 1130] The Ambrosian edition reads: “she falsely assumed the name of the Church, O deceitful cave.” The Erasmian edition reads: “then she will falsely assume the name of the Church, O Judaea of deceitful appearance.” The Lovaniensian edition reads: “you falsely assume the name of the Church, deceitful Judaea.” The readings have been corrected from the manuscripts. Here “cave” refers to the Arian Church, as also in the preceding treatise, chapter 7.], deceiving because you have been deceived. I see that you arrange your appearance under another’s guise. Why do you adorn yourself? Why do you decorate yourself so lavishly? Why do you spread out your fringes? Why do you strive to make yourself equal to the true bride?

The bridegroom does not receive you, because you are not the bride. But you say that you are beautiful and boast of gold and abundant ornaments. The bridegroom answers you—the one who is “beautiful beyond the sons of men” (Ps. 45:3–4): “The appearance of a prostitute has become yours; you have become shameless in everything.”

And if you should say, “Why?” he answers: “Because you arrange yourself under the appearance of a bride and falsely claim that I am your bridegroom. The appearance of a prostitute has become yours; you have become shameless in everything. You did not call me as [you call] the Father: ‘I and the Father are one’” (John 10:30). “You did not call me Father and the prince of your virginity” (Jer. 3:3–4).

These are Christ’s words through the prophet. For if I were the prince of your virginity, I would preserve your integrity, just as I preserved my mother’s integrity intact. Since, therefore, you acknowledge neither me as the prince of your virginity nor as equal to the Father, neither do I acknowledge you as a virgin.

Do not boast any longer that you are what you are not. Acknowledge your shame: Arius has taken away your integrity. You are therefore not the bride, because you are not whole. For you call him your bridegroom in vain when he is not yours; Christ does not take a shameful widow.

Return, return, rejected one; return, confounded one; return, violated by the serpent’s deceits. Return—not composed in heavenly divinity, but deceived by human assertions. Return. You can deceive yourself; you cannot deceive the bridegroom. For he knows the one whom he seeks, and recognizes the one whom he calls.

The mother always lives. Stepmother, why do you put yourself forward? You cannot exclude the beautiful mistress when you yourself are a shameful servant. “The appearance of a prostitute has become yours.” For you did not keep faith with one husband, since you do not hold the Catholic unity.

That bridegroom seeks a true mother who will piously nourish her children, not a shameful one who deceitfully kills the children of others. See what this true mother is: she still tolerates you while you strangle her children and inflict injuries upon her husband. She tolerates you because she displays her bridegroom’s patience and awaits the breezes of freedom, so that her humility may be avenged by him, since she possesses the love of her husband.

For he is the one who lives and reigns with God the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.

[Col. 1131]

# A Dialogue on the Dispute between the Church and the Synagogue

[Note: [Col. 1131] It has nothing of Augustine’s style; the author seems to have been some court official or jurist.] (C, G, S)*

[Col. 1131] I seem to have undertaken before you, my judges, the case of two matrons. I shall lay out the affairs of both at length, so that whatever truth, demanded by the judgment of your court, may have settled, one of the two may observe it. Therefore, in this assembly of yours, I recite the law and present the documents. Let the case be conducted according to law, since the dispute concerns possession; and I shall not delay in reviewing the judgments established by imperial sanction, so that whatever the order of truth has discerned may be promulgated according to the divinely given law as the judgment of your court.

At one time, one of them, caught in adultery, had violated the rights of our possession by prematurely invading it as a herald of her claim. The other, by the merit of chastity and through the sentence of the donor, had previously deprived that possessor—whose appearance before your ears seems to have been exacted—of certain things in the world through a clandestine fraud. She is compelled daily to return them by restitution, and she still owes as much as she has returned. For we renounce everything that she had claimed for the possession.

Therefore, if you wish to hear the aspect of the case, the face of the parable: the powerful and once gold-rich woman Synagogue invaded the Gentiles, our inheritance and possession, and the boundaries of the earth granted to us by august law. Soon we pleaded our case; we hold our petitions in our hands. The immediate introduction to the estate and the possession acquired remain under our right. Nevertheless, we do not wish to release whatever ornaments the restless woman seized. When she was required to return them, she paid them back more slowly than she ought.

Now, therefore, to this matron and widow, our matron—that is, to the Synagogue—

**CHURCH said:** Recite what you have deserved, and I shall recite what I have deserved.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** All the prophets came to me, something you cannot deny.

**CHURCH said:** It is certain that, when the prophets came to you, they ran to you as to a hostess, as though merely to delay for a time. For I prove that those same young men of my bridegroom—the surveyors, so to speak, the bearers of Christ’s writings and also the carriers of his commandments—were killed by you out of envy. If they had come to you, could any one of them have been killed by you? But because they were coming to me, and you could not bear to receive my people, whom jealousy had provoked, you attacked them with sword and clubs.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** Even if I did what you claim, I sinned rightly and honorably, because I knew the king whose letters I had often received. But you were being sought as a woodland dweller, one who, in the manner of barbarians, lived in the countryside and on the hills, among pathless or hidden places, once dwelling in a rustic hut. For what was ever more rustic than you? With the nations with whom I had often fought, you followed, I suppose, bleating sheep and cattle in pastoral fashion. I, supported by scepter and legions, reigned at Jerusalem clothed in purple. I possessed the Roman empire. I killed kings, soldiers, and commanders of foreign peoples. The Persian and the Indian brought me gold, gems, ivory, silver, silk, and all their riches. You were a mountain-dweller, rustic, suited to cattle; you dwelt anxiously only in deep valleys; you were hidden in a vast crag—[Note: [Col. 1131] Perhaps *condensaque*, “and dense”; or *contemptior*, “more despised.”—a fissured rock once offering a timid shelter—eating milk from cheese and bilberries with acorns. I killed Pharaoh in his chariots; I killed the Egyptians, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Hittites, and the Perizzite kings.

**CHURCH said:** I recognize what you say, and I cannot deny your praises. I know that you saw the splendid marketplaces and lofty Capitols of your city. The force of your arms, the gleaming emblems on your shields, the spears, swords, and javelins of hurled missiles, and the resounding groan of cavalry armies laid low great, richly adorned commanders and tyrants. I know your power, which that Jerusalem of pompous pride belched forth. For I know that once the Roman world trembled before you and the earth of the nations quivered.

But you must remember what you did at Shechem on account of one woman, Dinah: you devastated defenseless men, radiant with the honor of their innocence, in the manner of brigands (Gen. 34:26).

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** The power of a kingdom received boldness from the liberty granted to it. Do you think I sinned in this, if under my rule I stained whomever I wished, or perhaps killed my own rebels? He who gave the power to reign had certainly granted my dignity the freedom to do whatever I wished. Or tell me this: if the one who reigns by his own authority and possesses everything is not bound by law, must he not extend the power of his kingdom wherever he wishes?

**CHURCH said:** In this I rejoice: I have been exalted because I have been made higher than the exalted, and I have shattered the kingdoms of those who reign. And behold, beneath my feet you, once a purple-clad queen, now move about. He is the King of kings who has begun to rule over the one who once saw herself reigning.

You reigned, I admit. The Roman land lay beneath you; kings and princes fell. Whenever you engaged in battle, the captive enemy succumbed. Do not be angry if you, who were once mistress, now appear to have become my servant.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** Since you have proclaimed yourself with such an announcement, prove the servant, and I shall acknowledge the mistress.

**CHURCH said:** I have the documents. I recite the testament that your former scribe and prophet wrote and that Aaron signed in the presence of the magistrate.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I know that the Testament was written under my rule, but I wish to learn where the dictator of the book commanded me to serve.

**CHURCH said:** Read what was said to Rebekah when she gave birth: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be divided from your belly; one people will overcome the other, and the greater will serve the lesser” (Gen. 25:23).

Certainly, a little earlier you said that you, the greater, had reigned, triumphed, held the scepter, and possessed the purple; while I, the lesser, had once hidden in valleys or dwelt among rocky hills. You said that you shone with gold, ornaments, fine linen, silk, and noble gems, while I, the lesser, lived scarcely on the milk of cattle. I possessed sheep and cattle; you possessed soldiers.

Therefore, since I am lesser and poorer, while you, greater and rich, have been subjected to me, choose [Note: [Col. 1132] Perhaps *degas*, “may you live,” or “may you withdraw.”] to serve the lesser people.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I recognize the title of the Testament; I see the letters that I myself preserved in my treasury and library. But tell me how I serve you, when I still acknowledge my children to be free. They are free from business obligations; they have freedom to sail; they know no chains; no one tears apart a vineyard by digging it under the compulsion of labor. I do not know whether I am subjected to you in servitude.

**CHURCH said:** You recall the Testament, you recognize its letters, and still you do not accept servitude!

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** You tell me what you assert. I recognize Moses and hear him, and I cannot reject him; but I cannot understand how I serve you.

**CHURCH said:** You cannot change; you always deny and deceive; you always contend from falsehood. Certainly you said earlier that you had reigned, when the people of Israel held the place of imperial power [Note: [Col. 1132] Elsewhere: “had held an extensive empire.”].

If you still reign, acknowledge that you are free and not yet subjected to me in servitude. But if the Christian people rightly reign over the people of Israel, it is clear that you are a servant, not free, since I see you subjected to servitude.

Look upon the standards of the legions; attend to the name of the Savior; observe Christian emperors; and consider that you have been expelled from the kingdom. In accordance with the faith of the Testament that you preserve, confess this to us: you pay tribute to me; you do not attain imperial power; you cannot hold a prefecture. A Jew may not be a count. You are forbidden to enter the senate. You know no prefecture. You are not admitted to military service. You do not touch the tables of the rich. You have lost the order of spiritual gifts. Nothing is permitted to you; even for eating, we grant you only a few things, so that you may at least live badly.

Therefore, if you have been deprived of those things that are highest and foremost, read what was said to Rebekah when she bore twins: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be divided from your belly; one people will overcome the other, and the greater will serve the lesser.”

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** What, nevertheless, had I done, that the divinity should expel me from the kingdom and deprive me of imperial power?

**CHURCH said:** Since you sinned so grievously, the punishment of servitude should likewise be grievous and deserved under the threat of death; you can be neither servant nor free. For when Moses first received the two tablets engraved with the Decalogue on Mount Sinai [Note: [Col. 1133] From the Greek *charattō*, “I engrave.”], you asked for idols against God, saying to Aaron: “Make gods for us who will go before us” (Exod. 32:1).

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** Here I acknowledge that I, miserable creature, went astray. But destruction immediately overtook those who asked for idols, carrying them to the ultimate death of condemnation. What, then, did their descendants do, if those elders who had committed this deed immediately received the deserts of their punishment?

**CHURCH said:** I am certain that you have read it, but you cannot retain what you have read—and I recognize this very thing. But recall what is written: “Let the children of their children declare it, for the sins of their parents have increased in their children, and I will not release them, says the Lord” (Jer. 32:29). And elsewhere he says: “The parents ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge” (Ezek. 18:2).

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** In what do you glory, when under my rule you hold imperial power? Christ came first to me, or into my people.

**CHURCH said:** It was fitting that divine wisdom should anticipate everything that had to be established. For if Christ had come principally to me and had wished to reject you at the very arrival of his first birth, you would say today: “He did not come to me; I did not know what I should worship.” For if he had also deigned to come among my people, whom the prophets had called God, I would confess him.

He came to you. By the authority of his miracles he raised your dead; he made the mute speak; he restored the lame to their steps; he gave sight to the blind; he set paralytics free by releasing their limbs; he restored lepers to health. Yet with a profane mind you said that the one whom you had read to be God was not God.

Therefore, because I remember that you said the Savior and Lord had first come to you, I again contend against you on the basis of your own testimony. Read what Ezra wrote to you in the person of the Savior: “I came to my own, and my own did not receive me. What shall I do to you, Jacob? Judah was unwilling to hear me; I will transfer myself to another nation” (4 Esd. 1:24).

From this you see that you ought not to glory in having seen Christ. For it is a greater cause of guilt to see the one whom you should serve and to despise the one to whom you ought to owe servitude. Perhaps you could defend yourself if you said: “I did not know the Lord; I did not know that the prophets had spoken falsely.” Yet the prophets did speak, and you recognized the very Lord whom the prophets had sung about through his miracles, but you blasphemed him with a pitiful rejection. You see that you cannot excuse yourself from the guilt of so great a crime.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** The prophets had indeed said that he would come, the anointed one of God, the holy child from a virgin. But I was entirely ignorant of whether the Lord himself wished to come.

**CHURCH said:** Isaiah therefore rightly said: “Go and say to this people: ‘You will hear with your ears, and you will not understand; you will see with your eyes, and you will not recognize.’ For the heart of this people has grown dull; they have heard heavily with their ears and have closed their eyes, lest they perhaps see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, return, and I heal them” (Isa. 6:9).

Jeremiah also says: “They have abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves cracked cisterns that cannot hold water” (Jer. 2:13).

And what did the same prophet add? “The kite knew its time; the turtledove and the swallow, the cranes and sparrows, kept the times of their arrival; but my people did not know me” (Jer. 8:7).

I believe you have also read this in Solomon, who says: “The wicked seek me and do not find me; for they hated wisdom, and they did not receive the word of the Lord” (Prov. 1:28–29).

You see, therefore, that you rejected the Son of God with blasphemous eyes and a profane heart. If you read Isaiah, you read the prophets, and you frequently heard that Christ is God. Thus he says, so that I may answer you concerning both the virgin and the son, as you yourself mentioned: “A virgin will bear a son, and his name will be called Emmanuel,” which is interpreted, “God with us” (Isa. 7:14).

And David says: “Therefore God, your God, has anointed you” (Ps. 45:8). And in Genesis he says: “And God made man in his own image” (Gen. 1:27).

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I do not want the readings to carry you away in such applause. Turn instead to what I think may benefit me. Consider that you received neither the Law nor circumcision, in which sign the Gentile world is separated. Therefore I possess my sign, and I do not abandon the Law that Moses brought forth.

**CHURCH said:** You testify that you received the Law, but the Law of the Old Testament; whereas I received the new Law of the Gospels. And so that you may know that the old has been compressed by the new, read Isaiah, who says to you: “Those former things have passed away; behold, new things have come to be; now they will arise” (Isa. 43:19).

As for your claim that you received the sign of circumcision for the salvation of the people, today I prove that your folly was deceived. If eternity was granted through circumcision, you can see that you received the head but not the feet, and were mutilated in one eye or one hand; you lived half alive and half dead.

For if you say that your people are to be saved by the sign of your suffering, what will your virgins do? What will your widows do? What will even the mothers of the Synagogue do, if you testify that the sign of circumcision has benefited the people toward eternal life?

Therefore, it is not proper for you to have Jewish women. Men are circumcised, but women do not admit the foreskin; therefore they cannot be saved, if you are saved by circumcision. You see, then, that you can have Jewish men—that is, the circumcised—but I declare that women, who cannot be circumcised, are neither Jewish nor Christian, but pagan.

Listen; I shall teach you clearly the insignia of circumcision. If you could have received that circumcision, you would never have fallen into the disgrace of being expelled from the kingdom.

Consider what Jeremiah says: “Thus says the Lord to the Jewish men who dwell in Jerusalem: Renew yourselves among yourselves with renewal, and do not sow among thorns. Circumcise yourselves for your God, and circumcise the foreskin of your heart” (Jer. 4:3–4).

Moses himself says the same, whom you likewise followed, although he carried commandments for me: “In the last days God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, so that you may love the Lord your God” (Deut. 30:6).

And the Apostle Paul says: “You were circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, not in the stripping away of the flesh, but in the circumcision of Christ” (Col. 2:11).

What shall we say to these things, Synagogue? Behold, not circumcision of the flesh but of the heart was commanded—that is, so that you might cut away the vices of the heart, sever lust, remove the head of idolatry, and tear apart the garment of fornication. For the prophet says: “You committed adultery upon stone and wood” (Jer. 3:9).

You see, therefore, that you received circumcision not as a sign of salvation, but rather as a sign of shame and disgrace. For do you think that to be a sign which is covered by clothing, which is not brought forth out of modesty, which is recognized as owed only to a wife? I have often seen your workshop and your women, with their heads shaved and shorn bald, condemned upon asses.

Indeed, if that which dishonored an adulteress and, by violating a virgin, subdued her is a sign of salvation, a woman who shamefully played with the salvation of circumcision ought not to be condemned; nor should the man be punished who assaulted or even cast to death an adulteress subdued by the saving sign of circumcision.

I do not know whether that could have been a sign of salvation from which those guilty of crime are condemned. But my people, by bearing the sign of salvation on the forehead, defend the whole person—men and women—through the height of the mark, in chastity from on high and in public freedom.

[Col. 1135]

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I would like to learn where you received the sign of the forehead, or which prophet engraved upon the sign of sanctification this sign that you call the sign of the forehead.

**CHURCH said:** You have the prophet Ezekiel, who cries out at the presence of Majesty: “Go and kill, and do not spare your eyes. Do not show pity to the elders; kill young men, virgins, children, and women to the point of annihilation. But do not touch anyone upon whom the sign has been written on the forehead” (Ezek. 9:5–6).

The same prophet also says: “Go through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh and mourn over the iniquities committed in their midst” (ibid. 4).

Likewise, in the Apocalypse: “I saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand, and they had his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads” (Rev. 14:1).

You see, therefore, the sign given to me: the mark of the cross, which, after dismissing and abandoning you, the Savior’s passion adorned.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** When asked about the sign of the forehead, you put forward the sign of the cross, as though the most ancient prophets had proclaimed its insignia before the Savior came. Therefore tell me whether you have read that Christ would suffer and hang upon a cross.

**CHURCH said:** Listen, Synagogue—not so that you may be taught, but so that you may be punished. Attend to the Law, and you will find where the Savior prophetically prefigured the cross with outstretched hands.

For Isaiah says in the person of the Savior: “I stretched out my hands all day toward a disobedient people who contradicted me, who walked in ways that were not good, but after their sins” (Isa. 65:2).

Jeremiah also says: “Come, let us put wood into his bread” (Jer. 11:19).

And in Deuteronomy, since you used the Pentateuch: “Your Life,” he says, “will hang before your eyes day and night” (Deut. 28:66).

Likewise the Psalmist reports: “I cried out to you, Lord; all day I stretched out my hands toward you” (Ps. 88:10).

And in Numbers—that is, in your Law, which you had received first—he says that Christ would be suspended and hang upon the cross: “God is suspended not as a man, nor does he suffer threats as a son of man” (Num. 3:19).

And elsewhere the prophet says: “The Lord reigned from the wood” (Ps. 96:10).

Behold the miracles of the passion; behold the mirror of light; behold the wicked schemes of your people, by which they hung God, the Son of God, upon the cross.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I recall the events, and I likewise recognize the words, but who are you to appear to rebuke me? You were rustic; you were once a mountain-dweller; you were alien to God’s laws; you lived in the manner of the Gentiles. I dwelt in the Law; the prophets came to me and brought me commands and precepts.

**CHURCH said:** Listen, Synagogue; listen, widow; listen, abandoned one. I am what you could not be. I am the queen who deposed you from the kingdom. I am the bride who, abandoning idols, came down from the forest and the mountain, as your patriarch says: “Behold, the scent of my son is like the scent of a full field that the Lord has blessed” (Gen. 27:27).

From where do you come, virgin, with milk, with flowers, an undefiled young maiden, from the shadowy grove, a simple and joyful citizen, arranged in a snowy cloak? My bridegroom, beautiful beyond the sons of men, the King of kings, who adorned my head with a headdress and immediately clothed me in purple, received me as I came.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** How will you be able to prove that you are the bride and that Christ appears in the Law as the bridegroom?

**CHURCH said:** If the prophets had run principally to me, you would say today that I was ignorant of the Law, that I had no prophets, and that I did not know what had been written. Therefore recognize that you must be refuted by your own prophets.

Listen, then, to what the prophets commanded concerning the bridegroom and the bride. For the prophet Joel says: “Blow the trumpet in Zion; sanctify a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly; gather the people; sanctify the Church; summon the elders; gather the children and nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come forth from his chamber and the bride from her bridal room” (Joel 2:15–16).

For I am certain that you are that Jerusalem of which both the bridegroom and the bride are spoken, as David says: “And he himself, like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber, rejoiced like a giant to run his course. His going forth is from the summit of heaven, and his course reaches to its summit; no one is hidden from his heat” (Ps. 19:6–7).

And in the Apocalypse John says: “Come, I will show you the new bride, the bride of the Lamb.” And he carried me away in the spirit to a great mountain and showed me the holy city Jerusalem descending from heaven, possessing the glory of God (Rev. 21:9–11).

John himself also says: “The Lord God Almighty will reign; let us rejoice and be glad, and let us give him glory, because the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his wife has prepared herself” (Rev. 19:6–7).

You see, therefore, that through the Law she was called both bride and wife: bride because I promise that I will render faith to the Lord Savior; wife because, through the conception of Baptism, with the Spirit acting as husband, I shall produce children from my womb, swollen with the bath. In this childbirth of more gracious generation, spirit and soul are joined in a marital union.

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I wish to know this, lest you perhaps think that I have forgotten what you said, since I seem to examine everything. What is it that you claim the prophet said? What is it that he says in Deuteronomy: “Your Life will hang before your eyes day and night” (Deut. 28:66)?

**CHURCH said:** I do not speak or declare this in order to teach you, but so that the silence of doubt may not draw a line across the matter. For this reason I convict you from your own Testament.

The Savior hung upon the cross day and night—that is, during the day of Friday and through the night of that day until the Sabbath, when you said according to the Law that it was not permitted for a man to hang upon a tree.

Let these things meanwhile seem to have been said to you as you have acted. But for the case of truth and the knot of doctrine, consider what we say: “Your Life,” he says, “will hang before your eyes day and night.”

For in one day there were both day and night. The light of day was suddenly marked off by the nocturnal darkness of a horror of shadows. Thus, when the Savior was suspended on the wood, from the sixth hour of the day until the ninth hour there was darkness (Matt. 27:45); night took away the light, and a deadly and mournful darkness blinded the entire day.

You see, therefore, that in one day there were both day and night. Rightly, on account of this very passion, he says in Deuteronomy: “Your Life will hang before your eyes day and night.”

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** Therefore, if he was suspended on the cross, if he hung there, if he was killed, how did he rise again? How do you assert that he is alive, that he rose again, and that he sits in heaven at the right hand of the Father? Teach me, then, whether he conquered death and rose again, who appears to have been killed—but assign to me what you say from the prophets.

**CHURCH said:** Listen, miserable one; listen, most wretched one; listen, murderous woman, who still doubts the death of Christ and the resurrection. Read what David said in the person of the Savior in the fifteenth psalm: “You will not abandon my soul to the underworld, nor will you give your Holy One to see corruption.”

Who is holy if not Christ? Who is incorrupt if not the Son of God? As he says in the twenty-ninth psalm: “Lord, you brought my soul up from the underworld.”

Likewise, in the third psalm: “I slept and took sleep; and I arose, because the Lord received me.”

And again David says in the person of the Father to the Son: “Arise, my glory; arise: I will rise at dawn” (Ps. 57:9).

For “at dawn,” as he says, means after the third day: death trampled down and the underworld condemned, he returns alive from the dead, as the prophet says: “In the evening weeping will linger, and in the morning there will be joy” (Ps. 30:6).

[Col. 1137]

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I had asked one thing, and you introduced another. I have learned about the resurrection and have learned that he overcame the underworld. But since you said that the Lord Savior rose on the third day, I do not know whether this actually happened.

**CHURCH said:** I know that you remember, but you do not wish to confess what you know, as a matter of repentance. Error torments the conscience, and guilt removes memory.

Listen, then: Christ rose from the underworld on the third day in order to give us life. Read the prophet Hosea, who says: “He revived us on the third day” (Hos. 6:3).

And in Deuteronomy he says: “The Lord said to Moses: ‘Go down and sanctify my people; sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their clothing and be ready for the day after tomorrow,’ that is, for the day beyond tomorrow; ‘for on the third day the Lord will descend upon Mount Sinai’” (Exod. 19:10–11).

And in the Gospel he says: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah. For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster for three days and three nights, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights” (Matt. 12:39–40; Luke 11:29–30).

**SYNAGOGUE replied:** I recognize it; the things reported to me on the testimony of prophecy are true. Now I wish to know where Christ is, where he is hidden, he who rose from the earth. For I want to see whether, after the passion or after the resurrection, he possesses any power according to the prophets. For I have read that Elijah, the anointed of God, would come to save the people.

**THE CHURCH** said: “Then, wretched woman, confess what you cannot deny; and hear all that truth cannot conceal: the whole freedom of its splendor extends even to the heavens. Read Daniel, who says:

‘I was watching in a night vision, and behold, with the clouds of heaven there came one like a Son of Man; he came even to the Ancient of Days and stood in his presence, and those who attended presented him. And royal authority was given to him, and all the kings of the earth by lineage, and every glory served him; and his authority is eternal, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom is eternal, which shall not perish’ (Dan. VII, 13–14).”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “I cannot deny that the Anointed of God—that is, Christ—possesses glory. But tell me this: after he suffered and rose again, was he able to attain and retain that glory?”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Read the prophet Isaiah, who speaks in the person of the Savior:

‘Now I will rise up, says the Lord; now I will be glorified and exalted. Now you shall see; now you shall understand; now you shall be confounded. The strength of your spirit shall be vain; fire shall consume you’ (Isa. XXXIII, 10).

“David also says:

‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool. The Lord will send forth from Zion the rod of your power, and you shall rule in the midst of your enemies’ (Ps. CIX, 1–2).”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Then he is both God and the Son of God.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Certainly, foolish woman. He who is begotten from a human being is human; likewise, he who arises from God is plainly designated God.”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “I do not believe assertions; I want to be refuted by the Law. For I intend to listen not to you, but to the Prophets.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Consider what the Psalmist says, and you will know that the Lord is God the Savior:

‘Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee from his presence. As smoke vanishes, so let them vanish; and as wax melts before the fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God. Sing to God, sing praises to his name; make a way for him who ascends over the setting sun—the Lord is his name. He brings out the prisoners in strength, those who dwell in tombs’ (Ps. LXVII, 2–3, 5, 7).

“And again the same David says:

‘Rise up, Lord, and judge the earth, for you shall inherit among all the nations’ (Ps. XXXVII, 22).

“And elsewhere:

‘The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken’ (Ps. XLIX, 1).

“And:

‘A virgin shall bear a Son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel,’ which is interpreted, ‘God with us’ (Isa. VI, 9).

“And:

‘Therefore God, your God, has anointed you’ (Ps. XLIV, 8).

“You have, then, both God, and Lord, and King.”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “I acknowledge both God and Lord; but I want the claim that he is King proved to me.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Most foolish of women, if you confess that he is God, ought you not to acknowledge him as King? Or can God exist without having reigned? Every kingdom lies beneath God’s feet, and whatever kingdoms possess, God’s majesty possesses. Do you therefore doubt that he is King whom you plainly recognize as God?”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “I do not indeed doubt it, but I want Israel to be confirmed to me by the truth.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Read David, and you will find in the seventy-first Psalm:

‘O God, give your judgment to the King, and your righteousness to the King’s Son.’

“And in the seventy-second Psalm he says:

‘But God our King before the ages has worked salvation in the midst of the earth.’

“And in the second Psalm:

‘But I have been appointed King by him over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming his authority.’

“And through Malachi he says:

‘I am a great King, says the Lord, and my name shall be glorified among the nations’ (Mal. I, 14).

“And in the ninety-sixth Psalm:

‘The Lord has reigned; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad.’

“And elsewhere:

‘My heart has poured forth a good word; I speak of my works to the King’ (Ps. XLIV, 2).”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “You have anticipated me; I can answer nothing. I seem to have been condemned not by an assertion of words, but by the Law.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Ask whatever you wish, and I shall refute you from your own Testament.”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Certainly you say that you cannot deny that Christ is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Abraham was certainly a Jew; how, then, do you say that I am condemned?”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Good: you have now begun to exchange arguments, and by the twists of your parabolic speech to feel out the limbs of your crooked words. For both Peter and Paul, my preachers, were Jews; but they abandoned you and came together at the fountain of life and eternal grace.

“For Abraham, whom you have mentioned, when he was still a pagan and was smashing idols, hastened into friendship with the divine majesty. From there, already safe as God’s friend, he approached you again; but afterward God commanded him to return from you to the Gentiles—that is, to us.

“For in Genesis it says:

‘The Lord God said to Abraham: Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, and go to the land that I shall show you; and I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you, and I will magnify your name’ (Gen. XII, 1–2).

“You see, then, the command given to Abraham: that he should go out from his land, from his kindred, and from his father’s house; that he should come to the land of the Gentiles, become prince over the nations, and receive a great name.

“Likewise, in a figure of the Savior, Isaac blessed Jacob:

‘Nations shall serve you,’ he said, ‘and princes shall worship you; you shall be lord over your brothers, and the sons of your mother shall worship you’ (ibid. XXVII, 29).”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Then everyone has come to you, while I, who had so many and such great children and gloried in the multitude of my children, am despised as abandoned, though I was once the mother of peoples. Or, if you have been commanded in the Law to have more children, you must prove it from the Law.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Now you yield; now your ancient rigidity lifts itself up, and soon you will turn again to malice. For the Lord says:

‘Enlarge the place of your tent, and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings; strengthen your stakes still farther to the right, and extend them to the left. Your offspring shall possess the nations, and you shall inhabit deserted cities. Do not fear, for you have been vanquished; do not be afraid, for you have been accursed, because you shall forget eternal shame’ (Isa. LIV, 2–4).

“I was indeed accursed when I followed idols; I was confounded when I did not know the commands of divinity; I was barren because I did not possess Baptism, by whose authority I might nourish children for the Majesty. Now I have been exalted in children, and through the Lord Christ I have received eternal kingdoms.

“Rightly also in *Βασιλειῶν*—that is, *of Kingdoms*—it says:

‘The barren woman has borne seven, and she who had many children has grown weak’ (I Kings II, 5).

“And the Apostle sends letters to the seven Churches (Rev. II, 11).

“And Jacob took two wives: the elder, Leah, weaker in her eyes, a type of the Synagogue; and the younger, beautiful Rachel, a type of the Church. She remained barren for a long time, and afterward bore children and was blessed (Gen. XXIX, 23, 28).

“Rightly it says in Genesis:

‘And the Lord said to Rebekah: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be divided from your belly; one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger’ (ibid. XXV, 23).

“Likewise, through the prophet Hosea:

‘I will call the one who is not my people, “My people,” and the one who is not beloved, “Beloved”’ (Hos. II, 24), and so forth.”

[Col. 1139]

**Editorial note:** Here, in manuscript B, the *Altercatio* ends. Erasmus, the Lyon edition, the Venice edition, and the Louvain edition add:

“For there will be a time when, in the place where it is said, ‘Not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’ For in Isaiah also you read:

‘Your land is desolate; your cities have been burned with fire. Foreigners shall consume your country in your presence, and behold, it is desolate and overthrown by foreign peoples. The daughter of Zion shall be left like a shelter in a vineyard, and like a watchman’s hut in a cucumber field, and like a city under siege.’

“Now, then, if according to the Law you have been abandoned and desolated, what have I done? Because I believed the marriage documents, I received a great kingdom—which you too could undoubtedly have possessed, if you had not condemned yourself beforehand through the madness of crime and profane parricide. For you remember what your prophet Ezra cries out in your person, when you imposed a pitiful servitude upon your children:

‘Go, children, for I am a widow and abandoned. I raised you with joy; I lost you with mourning and sorrow.’”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Then have I committed murder?”

**THE CHURCH** said: “See whether you, persecutor of human blood, have incurred the charge of murder; for you cannot deny that you killed the righteous Prophets of God.”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Who proves to me that I stained my hands with the blood of the Prophets?”

[Col. 1140]

**THE CHURCH** said: “Your sword still drips with fresh blood from the tip of its point, and you desire to be refuted? Hear, then, what Elijah testifies:

‘With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord my Almighty, because the children of Israel have abandoned you, demolished your altars, and killed your Prophets with the sword; and I alone remain, and they seek my life to take it away.’

“See also what Ezra foretold:

‘They departed from you and went after your Law, and they killed your Prophets, who urged them to return to you.’

“Jeremiah likewise wrote:

‘I sent my servants the Prophets to you; I sent them before dawn, but you did not listen, nor did you incline your ears, lest you walk after foreign gods and serve them; and you were unwilling to hear my commandments.’”

**THE SYNAGOGUE** replied: “Now I recall; now I recognize. But what was said earlier I did not know, because I listened negligently to those Prophets.”

**THE CHURCH** said: “Not what you say, but what you have understood in the Law also appears to be the testimony, as Isaiah says:

‘All these words shall be like the words of a book that has been sealed. If you give it to a person who does not know letters to read, he will say, “I cannot read, for it is sealed.” But on that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book; and the eyes of the blind, those who are in darkness and in mist, shall see.’

“And as Jeremiah says: ‘On the last day you shall know him.’

“Daniel likewise wrote: ‘Make the words obscure; seal the book until the time of consummation, when many shall be brought in and knowledge shall be fulfilled; for when dispersion occurs, they shall understand everything.’

“All these things have been recognized, and everything has run happily in its proper order. Therefore know that you have been condemned by your own sword, struck down by your own Testament, by the utterances of your Prophets—that is, of all the Jews.

“For this purpose I have brought forward what I have shown, preserving the Gospels and the Apostles for myself and my people; if you had read them, you would have howled still more.

“Rejoice, peoples; rejoice, worshipers of Christ: the barren woman has borne, and she who had children has already failed together with her children.”

# ON FAITH AGAINST THE MANICHAEANS, ONE BOOK, ATTRIBUTED TO EVODIUS. (C, G, S)*

## NOTICE ON THE FOLLOWING BOOK

It is attributed to Augustine in earlier editions, but falsely, as Bellarmine, Vindingus, and others establish. For it is not listed among his minor works, neither in the *Retractations* nor in the Catalogue of Possidius. Its style also differs from Augustine’s, and its method of argument is weaker. Nevertheless, the author attempted to imitate Augustine and reproduced not only his ideas but sometimes his very words, especially from the book written against the Manichaeans *On the Nature of the Good*.

In ancient codices it is found immediately after Augustine’s *Treatise on Faith and the Creed*, with an annotation inserted that reads as follows in the eight-hundred-year-old Fossatensis codex:

“Here ends, in Christ Jesus the Son of God, the treatise of Aurelius Augustine, bishop, on the Catholic Faith. Here begins the work against the Manichaeans.”

If the punctuation of the words is considered, it is not easy to determine whether the work that ends or the one that begins is called the treatise *On the Catholic Faith*. We think that this circumstance caused the following book to be attributed to Augustine and to be entitled *On Faith*. In fact, this inscription suited the preceding book well, but not the following one; and other manuscript codices indicate that it belongs to the preceding book, since they have more accurate punctuation.

Most clearly this is shown by the extremely ancient Corbie manuscript, on whose authority Sirmond says in the first chapter of his *Predestinarian History* that this book belongs to Evodius, bishop of Uzalis. For after the closing formula attached to the preceding book—“Here ends, in the Lord Christ, the Son of God, the treatise of Aurelius Augustine on the Catholic Faith”—a space of approximately seven lines is left blank, and the title of the following book is displayed separately at the head of the next folio, as follows:

“Here begins his work against the Manichaeans.”

Whether “his” refers to the same author or to Saint Evodius is unknown. The Colbertine manuscript agrees with the Corbie manuscript, as do several other manuscripts, which likewise preserve uncertainty concerning Augustine and Evodius as authors.

## CHAPTER I

[Col. 1139]

There is one God, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, invisible, incomprehensible, ineffable, inviolable, undefiled, who alone possesses immortality and dwells in inaccessible light [Col. 1140] (I Tim. VI, 16); he himself is the true light, life and truth, good, supreme, and whatever human speech can proclaim about him—though these things are given by him so that they may in some manner be spoken. From him are all things, through him are all things, whether Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, or Powers; and all things were created through him and in him (Col. I, 16), as is manifested in both Testaments to the humble and devout who seek him. To him be glory and honor and power for ever and ever. Amen.

## CHAPTER II

This Manichaeus says has as its adversary some prince of the race of darkness, whoever he may be, whom he also asserts to be unbegotten and not to have an author by whom he was created. And certainly, if he is unbegotten and not created, he is immortal through himself; and if he is immortal through himself, he will not be God, since God alone possesses immortality; and the Apostle will now be a liar when he says of God that he alone possesses immortality (I Tim. VI, 16).

But because the Apostle is not a liar, God alone possesses immortality. Therefore he alone can grant immortality both to souls and to whatever bodies he wishes.

## CHAPTER III

It is therefore false that Manichaeus asserts that some nature of evil, together with its prince, has no author but is unbegotten. Further, if the unbegotten is God, and the race of darkness is likewise now unbegotten, then unbegotten and unbegotten, seeing and seeing, reigning and reigning, living and living, eternal and eternal will not be opposites.

And if evil is opposed to good, then good will differ from evil in some respect; but in many respects it will be joined and concordant with it, and it will no longer be pure evil, since it will possess so many good things in common with God.

If they say, “The unbegotten is in its own sphere,” they say nothing. For unbegotten and unbegotten, eternal and eternal, insofar as they are unbegotten and eternal, will never be opposites. Surely, because an emperor is great in his own authority, while a minor official is contemptible in his own activity, will the minor official therefore not be a human being because the emperor is a human being?

## CHAPTER IV

But if anyone asks what evil is, let him hear the Apostle saying:

“The root of all evils is greed; by pursuing it, some have strayed from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows” (ibid., 10).

## CHAPTER V

Greed, however, is present in each person not naturally but voluntarily. Therefore he said, “by pursuing it.” For what is possessed by pursuing it would not be possessed if it were not pursued.

The Lord also, showing that the matter lies within human power, says:

“Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad” (Matt. XII, 33).

In the *Acts* written by Leucius [Note: In printed editions, “by Leontius.” In the Vatican manuscript, “by Locutius.” In the Corbie, Cistercian, and certain other manuscripts, “by Leucius.” Compare the *Acts concerning Felix*, book 2, chapter 6.], which they themselves accept, it is written as follows:

“For even beautiful fabrications, pretended display, and the coercion of visible things do not proceed from their own nature, but from that human being who by himself has become worse through seduction.”

Manichaeus himself also could not help confessing that souls—even those whom he says belong to God’s substance—sin by their own will. For in the second book of the *Treasure* he says:

“But those who through their own negligence have by no means allowed themselves to be cleansed from the stain of the spirits mentioned above, and who have obeyed the divine commandments only imperfectly, and who have been unwilling to observe fully the law given to them by their liberator, and who have not governed themselves as was fitting, and so forth.”

Likewise, in the *Epistle of the Foundation*, he says concerning those souls that allowed themselves, through love of the world, to wander from their former luminous nature, became hostile to the holy light, openly armed themselves for the destruction of the holy elements, and obeyed the fiery spirit, afflicting through their hostile persecution the holy Church and the elect established within it, observers of the heavenly commandments:

“They are excluded from the blessedness and glory of the holy earth. And because they allowed themselves to be overcome by evil, they will remain in that same stock of evil, with that peaceful earth and those immortal regions forbidden to them. This will happen to them because they so entangled themselves in unjust deeds that they were separated from the life and freedom of the holy light. Therefore they will not be able to be received into those peaceful kingdoms, but will be fixed [Col. 1142] in that dreadful sphere, which must also be guarded.”

Hence, he says, the same souls will cling to those things that they loved, “left behind” [Note: The Vatican manuscript reads, “the light having been left behind.”] in the same sphere of darkness, acquiring this for themselves by their own merits. For they did not strive to know these future things, nor did they separate themselves from them when the opportunity was given.

## CHAPTER VI

I ask you: when these words are heard, do you still doubt that Manichaeus was compelled to confess that sin is a matter of one’s own will? For he did not say one word about it, but so many that they would awaken anyone sunk in deep sleep.

He said, “through their own negligence”; he said, “have by no means allowed”; he said, “have obeyed imperfectly”; he said, “have been unwilling to observe.” Again he said, “they obeyed”; he said, “they allowed themselves to be overcome”; he said, “they entangled themselves”; he said, “acquiring this for themselves by their own merits”; he said, “For they did not strive to know these future things, nor did they separate themselves from them when the opportunity was given.”

And do you doubt saying that people sin by their own will?

## CHAPTER VII

Again, in the same epistle he says: “The residual portion of the Light,” that is, sinful souls. And you do not say that anyone sins except the race of darkness?

But why should I speak of this man, who, although he was in error, was nevertheless compelled by the most evident truth to say this, when you refuse to understand our Lord Jesus Christ saying that the fire was prepared for sinners, for the devil and his angels (Matt. XXV, 41), whom he wished all to be understood as sinners?

For it is not unjust for God to condemn those who have sinned in no way at all.

## CHAPTER VIII

For what else is it to sin than not to remain either in the commandments of truth or in truth itself? If sinners do not do this voluntarily, they are judged unjustly.

That angels also belong to the judgment, the Apostle shows when he says:

“Do you not know that we shall judge angels?” (I Cor. VI, 3).

They would not belong to the judgment by which they are judged if they did not belong to the sin by which they become guilty; nor could they rightly be judged. For righteous human beings will not judge righteous angels, to whom they will be like, but sinful ones.

Each person, therefore, is the author of his own wrongdoing through desire.

## CHAPTER IX

It is therefore within one’s power whether desire exists; and for that reason evil too lies within one’s power. What ought not to exist in the will nevertheless lies within its power. For evil cannot be nature, substance, or life, because these are good insofar as they exist.

But even if we call some people naturally evil, we say this because of the origin of the ancient sin in which our mortality is now born. Everything, therefore, that is called evil in human beings is sin and punishment.

Sin is committed by a rational soul, which possesses freedom of will; punishment is inflicted by God’s justice, which does nothing unjustly. Against these truths the Manichaeans bark with their customary blindness. When they are proved that evil is not nature, but that it lies within human power to act well or badly, they say that the soul does not possess free will, and they do not see their own blindness.

## CHAPTER X

For who would not cry out that it is foolish to give commandments to someone who is not free to do what is commanded, and unjust to condemn someone who had no power to fulfill the commands? Yet these wretched people do not understand that they are attributing such injustices and iniquities to God.

But what is true except that the Lord gives commandments, souls possess free will, evil is not a nature but a turning away from God’s commandments, and God’s judgment by which he condemns sinners is just?

## CHAPTER XI

Meanwhile, although this same Manichaeus says that God is abundant in all good things, with no distinguished kingdom of his lacking anything or being weak, and that his splendid ages were so firmly founded that they could never be shaken or moved by anyone, shortly afterward, in another passage, he adds and says:

“But the Father of the most blessed Light, knowing the great stain and devastation that would rise from the darkness and threaten his holy ages, unless he set against it some exceptional and splendid divinity, powerful in virtue, which might at once overcome and destroy the stock of darkness, so that, once it had been extinguished, rest might be prepared for the inhabitants of the light.””

## CHAPTER XII

Certainly, then, the kingdoms of Manichaeus’s god could never be shaken or moved by anyone. For if they could, he lied when he said that those kingdoms could not be shaken by anyone.

And if they were shaken by necessity or fear, he will not be God, since he could be shaken in this way. For according to Manichaeus himself, we see Manichaeus’s god oppressed by the evil of necessity, when stain and devastation threatened his ages and he had no other course of action; he therefore sent his own portion into battle, so that in this way at least he might procure rest for the inhabitants of the light.

But this very portion of him—light from light, good from good, holy from holy, eternal from eternal, God from God, omnipotent from omnipotent—was corrupted, killed, and mingled throughout all the bodies of the world, from highest to lowest, from heaven to dung. Thus prostitutes in theaters and women even more depraved in baser places had within themselves a God who had been oppressed and perhaps could not be liberated.

For at the end of that very epistle, from which we have already cited one chapter, he says that this portion of God which has been mingled cannot all be restored to its original freedom.

## CHAPTER XIII

Behold the victory; behold the triumph that Manichaeus’s god achieved. For after losing his own portion, he is in mourning, as Manichaeus himself says: he has a veil against himself to moderate his grief, lest he see the corruption of his portion.

For today the divine substance of which he speaks is subject to the race of darkness like clay to the potter. This is written in the first book of their *Treasure*.

## CHAPTER XIV

What disgrace, meanwhile, did he write in the same *Treasure*, among its other obscenities, in the seventh book, saying:

“Then that blessed Father, who has luminous ships as inns and dwellings according to their sizes [Note: The Laudunensis Ecclesiae codex reads, “according to the size of themselves.” The Corbie manuscript, together with the Ambrosian edition, reads, “according to their sizes.” In *On the Nature of the Good*, chapter 44, it reads, “or sizes.”], in accordance with the clemency implanted in him, brings aid by which he is stripped and liberated from the impious bonds, constraints, and anguish of his vital substance.

“Therefore, by his invisible command, he transforms those virtues of his that are contained in this most brilliant ship, and makes them submit to the hostile powers that have been arranged in each region of the heavens.”

“Since these powers consist of both sexes, male and female, he therefore commands the aforementioned virtues, partly in the appearance of boys without clothing [Note: The Corbie manuscript, by a second hand, reads, “boys in clothing.”], to submit to the opposing race of females, and partly in the form of luminous virgins to the opposing race of males.

“For he knows that all the hostile powers, because of the deadly and most foul desire innate in them, are easily captured and enslaved by these same beautiful forms that appear, and dissolved in this manner.

“Know, moreover, that this same blessed Father of ours is also identical with his virtues, which for a necessary purpose he transforms into the undefiled likeness of boys and virgins. He uses them as his own weapons, and through them accomplishes his will.”

## CHAPTER XV

These divine virtues, which are established in the likeness of marriage against the infernal races and which accomplish at once, with eagerness and ease, whatever they have conceived, fill the luminous ships.

Therefore, when reason requires that these holy virtues appear to males, they immediately display their own image in the guise of most beautiful virgins. Again, when they come before females, they set aside the appearance of virgins and display the appearance of boys without clothing.

At this beautiful sight their ardor and desire increase, and in this way the bond of their worst thoughts is dissolved. The living soul that was held in their limbs is loosened on this occasion, escapes, and mingles with its own pure air. There, souls that have been thoroughly cleansed ascend to the luminous ships, which have been prepared for their transport and for their crossing to their homeland.
